ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.6 (individuals with significant control register); Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts 2.1 ff (ultimate beneficial ownership declarations to the Registraire des entreprises); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, and Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, CQLR c C-11, r 9.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Affidavit or statutory declaration as to source of funds and source of wealth of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths before whom the declarant executed the affidavit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and certificate of incorporation of any corporate shareholder, if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or registrar of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague registries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed power of attorney appointing the Quebec registered agent and/or the initial directors

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for execution outside Canada; consular legalization where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French or English translation of any non-English, non-French due diligence or corporate document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator accredited by the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ) or an equivalent recognized authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, officer, and individual with a power of attorney against the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC SDN List for all USD payment-rail and Stripe/PayPal/payment processor counterparty onboarding. FINTRAC-regulated service providers must apply Politically Exposed Person (PEP) determination for domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence where a PEP or higher-risk source of wealth is identified. Sanctioned persons and entities are immediate disqualifiers. Screening results and all source-of-wealth evidence must be recorded in the client due diligence file and retained for at least five years after the termination of the client relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Services; portal: registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, CQLR c C-11, r 9, the corporate name must be registered in French, or in French together with another language with the French version clearly dominant. Non-Latin scripts such as Cyrillic, Arabic, or CJK must be transliterated into Latin characters and must have a registered French form. A foreign trademark may remain in another language only if it is a registered trade-mark within the meaning of the Trade-marks Act, RSC 1985, c T-13, and is accompanied by a French counterpart where required. REQ's name system accepts Latin-character strings only for the official legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tout terme pouvant laisser croire a un lien avec la Couronne, un ordre professionnel, un ministère ou un organisme public
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a REQ name refusal the applicant should first obtain the written grounds for refusal. If the ground is similarity or non-distinctiveness, the applicant should file a new name reservation with a distinctive element and an updated REQ/NUANS search report. If the refusal is based on language policy, public order, or prohibited tokens, the applicant may file a written internal review request with the legal directorate of the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the refusal letter, the search report, any consent from the holder of a conflicting name, and a compliance argument addressing the Charter of the French Language. If the internal review is unsuccessful, judicial review may be commenced before the Court of Quebec within 60 days under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, arts 529 et seq., or, for a CBCA federal name rejection, by applying to the Director at Corporations Canada and thereafter to the Federal Court. In parallel, an alternative compliant name should be reserved to prevent incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this online maternity and infant care retail business, provided that the virtual office occupies or uses a physical street address in Quebec, is in the corporation's name under a written service agreement, and is capable of receiving notices, service of process, and correspondence from REQ, Revenu Quebec, the CRA, and creditors. A postal box or mail-forwarding-only address will not satisfy the head office and address for service requirements. No physical storefront or warehouse is required by the corporate or municipal licensing regimes for an e-commerce seller of maternity and baby supplies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 5% aggregate probability in the first year for a low-risk, online-only, non-regulated e-commerce business. Unannounced physical inspections are not routine at incorporation; they are generally triggered by inconsistent registry information, overdue annual declarations, Revenu Quebec or CRA audit flags, or a compliance complaint. If the company registers for GST/QST and grows above the e-commerce registration threshold, the likelihood of documentary or virtual inspections rises modestly, but remains below 15% annually.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 10-13, 98-153; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 17-30
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Direction de la publicite legale des entreprises, online at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (articles constitutifs) and mandatory registration statement (declaration d'inscription)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement. The corporation may authorize shares without par value. Lawful consideration, including cash, property, or past services, must be received before allotment and recorded in the share subscription ledger. Funds may be held in any Canadian chartered bank; no blocked capital account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned first directors, acting pursuant to section 98 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act, accept their appointment and assume office; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be fixed at [address], in the Province of Quebec, with the Enterprise Registrar as the competent registry; RESOLVED, that the corporation adopt its model by-laws and proceed with the allotment and issuance of common shares to the initial subscribers against lawful consideration recorded in the share subscription ledger; RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the board; RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute banking resolutions, tax registrations, and all filings necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online services at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Enterprise Registrar's centralized enterprise and legal person name database. Verify that the proposed corporate name is distinctive, lawful, and not confusing with existing names. If a trade name is desired, request a name report or name reservation valid for 90 days; alternatively, use the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) as the legal name of the corporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with legal element, e.g., [Company] inc.
Consent to use a reserved name, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the proposed name, file an amended name reservation request. Any final refusal may be contested by judicial review before the Court of Quebec within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Registration Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and legal counsel / notary; final filing with Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in the prescribed form, including the corporate name, registered office address, share capital structure, restrictions on share transfers, first directors, and any restrictions on business activities. Prepare the registration statement identifying the enterprise name, primary activity (NAICS 458110 / ISIC 4791), establishment address, and directors' information. Have signatures witnessed or notarized where paper filing is used; electronic filing requires compliant secure electronic signatures.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director of each first director
Subscriber or incorporator statutory declarations, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is deemed incomplete, cure the deficiencies indicated by the Registrar and resubmit within the prescribed administrative delay. If a substantive refusal is issued, file representations or amendments before seeking judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing, Payment, and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the articles of incorporation and registration statement through the Enterprise Registrar's online portal. Pay the official filing fee by credit card or authorized electronic method. The Registrar stamps the application with date and time of receipt, examines legal conformity, and issues the certificate of incorporation together with the enterprise number (NEQ). The corporation exists from the date and time set out in the certificate.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or authorization if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a refusal or query, respond with corrective information or amended documents within the stated period. After a final refusal, judicial review may be initiated before the competent Quebec court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Resolutions, By-Laws, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and initial shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions. Approve the corporation's by-laws, approve the issuance of common shares to initial subscribers, elect or confirm officers, authorize the corporate seal and banking resolutions, select the financial year-end, approve payment processor mandates (Stripe, PayPal), and open corporate bank accounts. Record all decisions in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
Share subscription ledger and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If by-laws are inconsistent with statute, amend them by board or shareholder resolution. If share issuance contravenes pre-emptive rights, obtain written waivers from affected shareholders and ratify the allotment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Ancillary Statutory Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec; Canada Revenue Agency; Registraire des entreprises; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with Revenu Quebec for QST and income tax accounts, with the Canada Revenue Agency for the business number, GST/HST account, and payroll deductions if employees are hired, and with CNESST for workers' compensation. Ensure the initial annual declaration due date is monitored. If a physical office or warehouse is used, complete municipal business licence and fire safety applications.
required_dossiers: Directors' identification information for tax filings
Lease or occupancy permit if physical premises are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations may be regularized by filing arrears returns and paying administrative penalties. Use voluntary disclosure procedures with Revenu Quebec and the CRA to obtain penalty relief for non-deliberate omissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no provincial industrial or manufacturing permit is required for online retail of maternity and infant care commodities; municipal authorities regulate any physical commercial premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; the mandatory public-law formality is enterprise registration with the Registraire des entreprises. A municipal business permit may be required only if an office or warehouse is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - online retail and distribution activity does not require a full EIA or environmental authorization in the absence of manufacturing, effluent discharge, or hazardous waste operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a fulfillment warehouse is operated, comply with municipal wastewater and zoning by-laws, the Quebec Clean Air Act, and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act where vehicle fleets or building equipment trigger applicable thresholds. No industrial wastewater discharge authorization is expected for packing-only operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any leased office or warehouse, obtain municipal fire safety certification, comply with Quebec Construction Code structural load requirements, and complete CNESST occupational health and safety registration if workers are employed. Online-only operations without employees or physical premises require no fire safety or workplace clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal; Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec provincial corporate tax and QST — Registre des entreprises du Québec (NEQ) and Mon compte RQ.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a CA_CORP business corporation: (1) obtain Articles of Incorporation (federal or Quebec); (2) receive the 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA upon incorporation; (3) register program accounts via BRO — RT (GST/HST) account, RC (federal corporate income tax) account, and RP (payroll) if employees are engaged; (4) register with Revenu Québec for the NEQ (10-digit enterprise number), Quebec corporate tax registration, and a QST account (TVQ) using the combined federal-provincial registration form or RQ Form LM-1/VF; (5) for non-resident vendors without a Canadian presence, use CRA Form RC1/RC1A interim-BN procedure and RQ non-resident registrant procedures, then apply for GST/HST and QST accounts once the CAD 30,000 registration threshold is met or exceeded, or voluntarily to claim input tax credits; (6) maintain the BN, NEQ, and program account numbers in billing systems, e-commerce platforms, bank account records, and contractual counterparty files.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian business corporation is a separate resident taxpayer subject to federal Part I corporate income tax and Quebec corporate income tax; no pass-through treatment for corporate shareholders; dividends are taxed at the shareholder level with applicable integration mechanisms. A Quebec-resident corporation's taxable income is computed federally (T2 return) and mirrored for Quebec Form CO-17 purposes, with separate provincial tax attributes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists; entity classification is determined by domestic law and applicable tax treaties. Available elections and statutory mechanisms include: Income Tax Act s. 39(6) functional-currency election; s. 216 election for non-residents to be taxed on net rental income; s. 217 election respecting certain non-resident withholding taxes; s. 85/88 rollover elections for tax-deferred corporate reorganizations and wind-ups; Excise Tax Act (ETA) s. 156 election for nil consideration supplies between closely related corporations; ETA s. 179 election for financial services; and equivalent QST elections under the Quebec Taxation Act (LTVQ). Anti-hybrid rules under ITA ss. 18.2–18.4 and 95.2, effective 1 January 2023, neutralize deduction/non-inclusion and dual-deduction mismatches and must be reviewed before any cross-border financing, licensing, or intellectual-property structure is adopted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST — dual value-added tax systems in Quebec: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5%, administered by CRA, and provincial Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at 9.975%, administered by Revenu Québec; Quebec is not an HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of world-wide taxable supplies (GST/HST and QST combined basis for small-supplier status) in any single calendar quarter or over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; below this threshold registration is voluntary; digital-platform vendors must also assess the deemed-supplier rules for marketplace sales and fulfilment-warehouse arrangements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API e-invoicing clearance regime is currently in force in Canada or Quebec. Registered suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed information under ETA s. 223 and equivalent Quebec QST invoicing rules; electronic invoices are valid where the recipient consents or where the marketplace/platform arrangement so provides. CRA's Budget 2024 roadmap proposes mandatory e-reporting and e-invoicing in phased implementation after 2026. Digital-platform economy reporting (PAN) rules effective 1 January 2024 require platform operators to report seller income and tax identifiers to CRA (Form RC385) and Revenu Québec; vendor business numbers and residence status must be verified by the platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST/HST and QST applies to goods exported by the vendor (ETA Schedule VI, Part V; QST Schedule III, Part V) where: (1) the supply is made to a non-resident purchaser; (2) the goods are removed from Canada as soon as reasonably practicable after the supply is completed; (3) the vendor obtains contemporaneous, credible documentary evidence of export before the filing of the applicable return; and (4) the evidence is retained for at least six years. For online e-commerce shipments, delivery to a foreign address by courier, freight forwarder, or postal service with customs declaration satisfies the proof-of-export requirement. Services may be zero-rated where performed wholly outside Canada or supplied to a non-resident recipient and not related to Canadian real property, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or services to persons in Canada; maternity and infant-care digital advisory or platform services must be reviewed against the specified digital services rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or an authorized courier/low-value shipment manifest exemption
Commercial Invoice / Canada Customs Invoice identifying exporter, consignee, and foreign destination
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or courier consignment note evidencing delivery outside Canada
Proof of payment from the non-resident purchaser, including Stripe, PayPal, or bank settlement records and foreign-currency conversion documentation

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds (best practice and commonly requested by Canadian banks under AML/KYC procedures, though not a statutory GST/QST condition)
Revenu Québec QST export substantiation file, including invoice-level export worksheets supporting the 0% QST rate on the provincial return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny the 0% rate and reassess at the combined 14.975% (5% GST + 9.975% QST) plus interest where export documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or insufficient; limitation periods are extended in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud. Civil penalties under ETA s. 280.1 (and Quebec equivalents) equal to 50% of the overclaimed refund or rebate may apply where a person knowingly, or under circumstances of gross negligence, makes a false statement or omission; criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 285 and ITA s. 239(1) (mirrored in Quebec's Tax Administration Act) carries fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to five years on indictment. Retrospective clawbacks of zero-rated export claims, denial of input tax credits, and disclosure obligations under the Voluntary Disclosures Program are available compliance-softening routes only before an audit is commenced by the tax authorities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible, and Canada imposes no exchange controls or split-currency conversion regimes. Current-account and capital-account transactions, including profit remittances, do not require central bank approval. Non-resident investors may freely repatriate capital, dividends, interest, and royalties, subject only to domestic withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (for interest, dividends, rents, royalties) and arm's length transfer pricing compliance under Section 247. Quebec corporate law adds no additional repatriation restriction. In-bound investment screening by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada applies only to acquisitions of control of a Canadian business above the WTO enterprise value threshold, which is inapplicable to a greenfield e-commerce establishment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not mandate surrender, conversion, or forced repatriation of export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in Canadian or offshore accounts. For tax and statistics purposes, the exporter must track transaction values in Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate, report monthly export data through the Canadian International Merchandise Trade regime where applicable, and retain all underlying invoices for a minimum of six years for Canada Revenue Agency and FINTRAC review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW as a licensed account-holding vehicle; MEDIUM as a payment gateway only. Offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) are not a recognized chartered bank category in Canada and cannot hold deposit accounts for corporate treasury without being registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). In Quebec, an EMI would also need recognition under the Money-Services Business Act (chapter M-30.1) and, if it lends or takes deposits, a Quebec financial services licence. Products such as Wise Business or Payoneer can be used as borderless pay-out channels, but settlement risk is borne by the corporate treasury and their balances are not eligible for CDIC deposit insurance. For the target e-commerce business, the most compliant design is to use a tier-1 Canadian bank as the master treasury account and route cash inflows through PCI-compliant cross-border payment providers (Stripe, PayPal) that fund into that account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are not statutorily required to be physically present in Canada for corporate account opening. Tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding through a video call and digital identity verification, but require certified corporate documents (Québec enterprise register extract, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership register) and a wet-ink or digital signature. For non-resident directors, a notarized or apostilled power and a passport-grade identity check are mandatory. Each bank maintains the right to require an in-branch interview for enhanced due diligence, and Quebec-heavy institutions may ask for a face-to-face interview in Montreal if the corporate profile presents unusual foreign ownership layers or high-risk payment flows. The required compliance package includes: (1) certificate of incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act; (2) registraire des entreprises attestation of incorporation with Quebec; (3) beneficial ownership table with 25% UBO identification; (4) proof of registered office address; (5) audited or unaudited financial statements; (6) board resolution designating banking signatories; (7) corporate tax identification number and applicable GST/QST registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction funding or remittance counterparty exposure (e.g., payments from OFAC-flagged or EU non-cooperative territories)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and AML screening policy; beneficial ownership chart; commercial invoices and customs documentation; risk-based customer due diligence file; FINTRAC suspicious transaction monitoring logs; legal source of funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered business activity (online retail of maternity and infant commodities) and receivable or payable flows (e.g., high-value commodity trades or cash-intensive payment processors)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed financial statements; audited revenue breakdowns; statement of final beneficial owners; e-commerce platform service agreements (Stripe/PayPal); IP address and delivery tracking evidence; bank reference letters from overseas correspondents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders creating ambiguity on economic substance in Quebec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Non-resident UBO passport copies; proof of Quebec/NCR permanent establishment; payroll and office lease records; statutory registers; tax return filings and provincial transfer pricing documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder loans and equity injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 messages through a correspondent bank to the Quebec operational account or capital escrow account held at a Schedule I bank. The wire should reference Canada's interbank payment clearing code (the 9-digit Canadian bank code and 5-digit institution/transit number) or use the Canadian route on SWIFT (CA). Inbound funds require the following: SWIFT purpose code TRFR (for transfers not related to trade) or used 'PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL' in field 70; supporting remittance letter; and for amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, FINTRAC's Large Cash Transaction Report rules apply only to cash, but international electronic funds transfer (ETFs) of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by financial intermediaries to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA. CRS/FATCA notification of account holder foreign tax status may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payment to overseas suppliers of maternity and infant commodities, the appropriate clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers against invoice, (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) at sight or deferred payment for substantial purchase orders, and (iii) Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) as a lower-cost alternative for shipments of high-value goods enumerated under HS Chapter 96 or similar. Open account with wire is acceptable for established suppliers. Outbound wires must include the intended trade-purpose descriptor, and the underlying commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin (if required) must be retained for CRA and customs verification. CAD, USD, EUR, and RMB clearings are available in Montreal through schedule I banks and correspondent networks in Hong Kong or Singapore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD FX forwards executed with a Schedule I bank, maturities aligned to trade payment cycles, subject to the bank's ISDA Master Agreement or Canadian FX master agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency pairs relevant to Asian supplier markets (e.g., CNY/INR/VND) when local deliverability is not possible, documented under the bank's derivatives terms and subject to OSFI counterparty credit limits
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for multi-currency shareholder loans or supplier credit arrangements, reported through a recognized Canadian trade repository under applicable derivatives reporting rules
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put) for hedging known transaction exposures, provided the options are not speculative and board-approved treasury policy specifies hedging-only intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; online filing available through Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may be subject to administrative fees; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Director to dissolve the corporation administratively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of registration or incorporation in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply; after two consecutive years of default, REQ may strike off the registration and the corporation loses legal existence in Quebec.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory minimum revenue or asset thresholds for a private Canadian corporation; an independent audit is compulsory if the corporation is a distributing/reporting issuer, if shareholders require the appointment of an auditor, or if the articles, by-laws, or unanimous shareholder agreement require it. Otherwise the audit may be waived by unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS, or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private companies; financial statements prepared under Canadian GAAP, with tax-basis reconciliation for CRA filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For CBCA corporations, maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it within 15 days of knowledge of a change. For Quebec, the annual declaration to REQ confirms ultimate beneficiaries and any 25%-or-more direct or indirect control; changes to Quebec UBO disclosure must be reported to REQ within 30 days, and the federal ISC register must remain available for inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (CBCA)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 185–925 (CAD 250–1,250) per year for Quebec registered office or registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–8,000 when an audit is required; most private companies can waive the audit, making the actual annual cost USD 0

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
